the brain acts in a complex and integrative way, so that it is not possible to attribute a specific function to a specific brain structure, and that the brain is not able to process and store information in a simple way, but that it is able to process and to store information on the basis of complex and sophisticated neuronal networks and codes.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain processes mnemonic information in a highly integrative way, which may be disturbed after circumscribed brain lesions, but that the integrative action of the brain is not disturbed by circumscribed brain damages.
the brain acts as a system which processes and integrates mnemonic information on the basis of an extensive and widely distributed network.

in the intact brain, mnemonic information processing is based on a wide-spread, integrative network of brain structures and neuronal connections, whereas in case of damage to circumscribed brain regions, the integrative action of the brain is impaired.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to look beyond the lesioned structure and to take into account the integrative action of the brain.

, in the case of brain lesions, the observed changes in mnemonic information processing cannot simply be attributed to the damaged structure but have to be understood in the light of the brain's integrative way of functioning.
